## Step 0: Build the SingleCellExperiment (SCE) input for MultiNicheNet

No `.h5ad` reload, no re-mapping of `cell_ontology_class`, no re-QC: `seurat_combined_filt`, `meta` (with `meta$final_celltype` already collapsed AND restricted to `target_celltypes`) and `keep_cells` are taken exactly as they exist at the end of `WGCNA_24_hdwgcna_HVG.Rmd`. This guarantees MultiNicheNet analyzes the identical cells, the identical cell type definitions, and the identical cell type restriction that WGCNA used for its pseudobulk network -- there is no risk of the two analyses silently drifting apart.

`colData(sce)` is still built explicitly (instead of relying on `Seurat::as.SingleCellExperiment()`), because that automatic conversion was found to silently drop most metadata columns in this project (only 3 columns were carried over instead of the expected 26). Building `colData` directly from `seurat_mnn@meta.data`, aligned by cell name, guarantees every column -- including `sex` and `tech` -- ends up in the SCE.

```{r}
heart_facs    <- ad$read_h5ad("D:/SandraAnjo/Luis Grilo/WGCNAandothersOlaia/data/Heart_facs.h5ad")
heart_droplet <-ad$read_h5ad("D:/SandraAnjo/Luis Grilo/WGCNAandothersOlaia/data/Heart_droplet.h5ad")

# var_names is already the gene symbol
facs_genes    <- rownames(py_to_r(heart_facs$var))
droplet_genes <- rownames(py_to_r(heart_droplet$var))
shared_genes  <- intersect(facs_genes, droplet_genes)
cat("Shared genes:", length(shared_genes), "\n")

combined_heart <- ad$concat(
  list(heart_droplet, heart_facs),
  axis = 0L,
  join = "outer",
  keys = c("droplet", "facs"),
  label = "tech",
  index_unique = "-"
)
combined_genes <- py_to_r(combined_heart$var_names$values)
combined_cells <- py_to_r(combined_heart$obs_names$values)

cat("Combined genes:", length(combined_genes), "\n")
cat("Combined cells:", length(combined_cells), "\n")

stopifnot(length(combined_genes) == ncol(combined_heart$X))
stopifnot(length(combined_cells) == nrow(combined_heart$X))

counts_matrix <- Matrix::t(as(combined_heart$X, "CsparseMatrix"))

sanitized_genes <- gsub("_", "-", combined_genes)
dup_idx <- duplicated(sanitized_genes) | duplicated(sanitized_genes, fromLast = TRUE)
if (sum(dup_idx) > 0) {
  cat("Genes affected by sanitization collisions:", sum(dup_idx), "\n")
  print(data.frame(original = combined_genes[dup_idx],
                   sanitized = sanitized_genes[dup_idx]))
}
final_genes <- make.unique(sanitized_genes)
stopifnot(sum(duplicated(final_genes)) == 0)
stopifnot(length(final_genes) == nrow(counts_matrix))

final_cells <- as.vector(combined_cells)
stopifnot(is.null(attributes(final_cells)))

rownames(counts_matrix) <- final_genes
colnames(counts_matrix) <- final_cells

metadata <- py_to_r(combined_heart$obs)
metadata <- as.data.frame(metadata, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
rownames(metadata) <- final_cells

# 'tech' should have exactly 2 levels (facs/droplet)
cat("'tech' values (real technology):\n")
print(table(metadata$tech))

# Rename the original 'batch' column: it's an internal sequencing batch,
# not the FACS/droplet technology
if ("batch" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
  metadata$seq_batch <- metadata$batch
  metadata$batch <- NULL
}

# sample_id is built from mouse identity (or sex+age as fallback), WITHOUT
# tech, so that metacells merge cells from both sequencing technologies
# for the same mouse / same age-sex point. This relies on 'harmony' as the
# integration reduction in MetacellsByGroups() to correct for tech-driven
# batch effects when averaging cells into metacells.
if ("mouse.id" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
  metadata$sample_id <- as.character(metadata$mouse.id)
} else {
  metadata$sample_id <- paste(metadata$sex, metadata$age, sep = "_")
}

cat("Numero de sample_id unicos:", dplyr::n_distinct(metadata$sample_id), "\n")
table(metadata$sample_id)

cat("Do counts_matrix and metadata match?",
    identical(rownames(metadata), colnames(counts_matrix)), "\n")
stopifnot(identical(rownames(metadata), colnames(counts_matrix)))

seurat_combined <- CreateSeuratObject(
  counts = counts_matrix,
  meta.data = metadata,
  project = "WGCNA_Mouse_Combined"
)
# QC thresholds 
min_features <- 200
n_before <- ncol(seurat_combined)

seurat_combined <- subset(
  seurat_combined,
  subset = nFeature_RNA > min_features 
)
cat("Cells before QC:", n_before, "\n")
cat("Cells after QC:", ncol(seurat_combined), "\n")

# Remove genes detected in very few cells globally
min_cells_gene <- 3
detected_genes <- Matrix::rowSums(GetAssayData(seurat_combined, layer = "counts") > 0)
genes_to_keep <- names(detected_genes[detected_genes >= min_cells_gene])

cat("Genes before filter:", nrow(seurat_combined), "\n")
cat("Genes after filter:", length(genes_to_keep), "\n")

seurat_combined <- subset(seurat_combined, features = genes_to_keep)
seurat_combined_raw<-seurat_combined
seurat_combined_filt_raw<-subset(seurat_combined_raw, subset = cell_ontology_class != "nan")

celltype_map <- c(
  "endothelial cell of coronary artery" = "EndothelialCells",
  "aortic endothelial cell"             = "EndothelialCells",
  "atrial myocyte"                      = "Myocytes",
  "ventricular myocyte"                 = "Myocytes",
  "fibroblast of cardiac tissue"        = "Fibroblasts",
  "leukocyte"                           = "Leukocytes", 
  "smooth muscle cell"                  = "SmoothMuscleCells", 
  "endocardial cell"                    = "EndocardialCells"
  # mast cell, valve cell -> excluded on purpose (not in this vector = dropped)
)

meta_raw <- seurat_combined_filt_raw@meta.data
meta_raw$cell_ontology_class_clean <- trimws(tolower(as.character(meta_raw$cell_ontology_class)))

names(celltype_map) <- tolower(names(celltype_map))
meta_raw$final_celltype <- celltype_map[meta_raw$cell_ontology_class_clean]

unmapped <- sort(unique(meta_raw$cell_ontology_class[is.na(meta_raw$final_celltype)]))
cat("Unmapped / excluded cell_ontology_class levels (dropped from analysis):\n")
print(unmapped)

cat("\nCells per final cell type:\n")
print(table(meta_raw$final_celltype, useNA = "ifany"))

DefaultAssay(seurat_combined_filt_raw) <- "RNA"
all_genes <- rownames(seurat_combined_filt_raw)
expr <- as.matrix(GetAssayData(seurat_combined_filt_raw, layer = "counts")[all_genes, ])

# keep only cells that were successfully mapped to a final cell type
keep_cells <- rownames(meta_raw)[!is.na(meta_raw$final_celltype)]
meta_keep  <- meta_raw[keep_cells, ]
expr_keep  <- expr[, keep_cells]

age_per_mouse <- meta_keep %>%
  distinct(sample_id, age) %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  mutate(n_ages = n()) %>%
  ungroup()

stopifnot("Some mice have more than one 'age' value -- inspect age_per_mouse" =
            all(age_per_mouse$n_ages == 1))

age_lookup <- setNames(as.character(age_per_mouse$age), age_per_mouse$sample_id)

# as.factor() sorts levels alphabetically ("18m" before "3m"), which
# scrambles chronological order -- build the ordered levels from the
# numeric part of the label instead, exactly as in the metacell workflow.
ordered_age_levels <- unique(age_lookup)
ordered_age_levels <- ordered_age_levels[
  order(as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", ordered_age_levels)))
]
```

```{r mnn-build-sce}
seurat_mnn <- seurat_combined_filt_raw[, keep_cells]

seurat_mnn$final_celltype <- meta_keep[colnames(seurat_mnn), "final_celltype"]
seurat_mnn$sample_id      <- meta_keep[colnames(seurat_mnn), "sample_id"]
seurat_mnn$age            <- as.character(meta_keep[colnames(seurat_mnn), "age"])
seurat_mnn$sex            <- meta_keep[colnames(seurat_mnn), "sex"]
seurat_mnn$tech           <- meta_keep[colnames(seurat_mnn), "tech"]  # "facs" or "droplet"

cat("Cells in the MultiNicheNet input object:", ncol(seurat_mnn), "\n")
cat("\nCells per final_celltype:\n"); print(table(seurat_mnn$final_celltype))
cat("\nCells per age:\n"); print(table(seurat_mnn$age))
cat("\nCells per sex:\n"); print(table(seurat_mnn$sex))
cat("\nCells per tech:\n"); print(table(seurat_mnn$tech))
cat("\nMice (sample_id) per age:\n")
print(table(unique(data.frame(sample_id = seurat_mnn$sample_id, age = seurat_mnn$age))$age))

# MultiNicheNet needs raw counts (it pseudobulks internally via muscat/edgeR),
# not the already log-normalized data used by WGCNA.
counts_mat <- Seurat::GetAssayData(seurat_mnn, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")

# Explicit colData, aligned by cell name -- do NOT rely on as.SingleCellExperiment()
col_data <- S4Vectors::DataFrame(seurat_mnn@meta.data[colnames(counts_mat), ])

sce <- SingleCellExperiment::SingleCellExperiment(
  assays  = list(counts = counts_mat),
  colData = col_data
)

cat("\nSCE dimensions (genes x cells):", dim(sce), "\n")
cat("Columns in colData(sce):", ncol(colData(sce)), "\n")
stopifnot(all(c("final_celltype", "sample_id", "age", "sex", "tech") %in% colnames(colData(sce))))
```

## Step 0b: drop age levels with too few biological replicates

`multi_nichenet_analysis()` fits its per-celltype pseudobulk model across **all** age levels present in `colData(sce)` at once, not only the two levels involved in a given contrast. An age level backed by a single `sample_id` (mouse) cannot have its between-replicate variability estimated, which breaks DE estimation for every cell type, not just that level -- this must be filtered out before any contrasts are built; no `min_cells` value can fix a lack of biological replicates.

```{r mnn-filter-low-replicate-ages}
min_samples_per_group <- 2

samples_per_age <- as.data.frame(colData(sce)) %>%
  distinct(sample_id, age) %>%
  count(age, name = "n_samples")

print(samples_per_age)

valid_ages <- samples_per_age %>%
  filter(n_samples >= min_samples_per_group) %>%
  pull(age)

dropped_ages <- base::setdiff(unique(colData(sce)$age), valid_ages)
cat("\nAge levels dropped for having <", min_samples_per_group, "samples:",
    paste(dropped_ages, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Age levels kept:", paste(valid_ages, collapse = ", "), "\n")

sce <- sce[, colData(sce)$age %in% valid_ages]

# Drop unused factor levels everywhere they could linger
colData(sce)$age       <- droplevels(base::as.factor(colData(sce)$age))
colData(sce)$sample_id <- droplevels(base::as.factor(colData(sce)$sample_id))

# Keep ordered_age_levels (from WGCNA_24) in sync with what actually survives here
ordered_age_levels <- ordered_age_levels[ordered_age_levels %in% valid_ages]

cat("\nRemaining cells:", ncol(sce), "\n")
cat("Remaining age levels (chronological order):", paste(ordered_age_levels, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Step 1: Define a single age contrast

`ordered_age_levels` is reused from `WGCNA_24_hdwgcna_HVG.Rmd` (same chronological order used there for `mouse_age`). Instead of generating every pairwise age combination (10 contrasts x 2 directions in the original version), **exactly one contrast is analyzed here: oldest vs. youngest** -- the two extremes of the aging trajectory. This keeps `multi_nichenet_analysis()` fast, and keeps every downstream section (circos plot, LR dotplot, WGCNA-overlap validation, hub-gene ligand activity) consistently about the same single comparison, instead of mixing results from 10 different age-vs-age models.

If you want a different pair of ages, edit `contrast_age_pair` below (it must contain exactly 2 values, both present in `ordered_age_levels`) -- everything downstream (contrast string, `youngest_age`/`oldest_age`, circos plot, validation) adapts automatically.

Before building the contrast, the age labels themselves need fixing: `multi_nichenet_analysis()` requires every group label in `colData(sce)[, group_id]` to be a syntactically valid R name (see `make.names()`), and labels such as `"1m"`, `"3m"`, `"18m"` start with a digit and therefore are not valid.

```{r mnn-fix-age-names}

# make.names() would auto-prefix "1m" -> "X1m", which is inconsistent with
# how ordered_age_levels was defined in WGCNA_24_hdwgcna_HVG.Rmd -- relabel
# explicitly instead, using the same mapping in both the age vector and the
# SCE colData.

age_recode <- setNames(
  paste0("age", ordered_age_levels),
  ordered_age_levels
)
print(age_recode)

# Relabel the chronological order already used in WGCNA
ordered_age_levels <- base::unname(age_recode[ordered_age_levels])

# Relabel the age column inside the SCE colData
colData(sce)$age <- age_recode[as.character(colData(sce)$age)]

cat("\nAge levels in colData(sce) after the fix:\n")
print(table(colData(sce)$age))

stopifnot(all(make.names(colData(sce)$age) == colData(sce)$age))

# Reference points reused later (circos plot, validation section, etc.)
youngest_age <- ordered_age_levels[1]
oldest_age   <- ordered_age_levels[length(ordered_age_levels)]
cat("\nYoungest age level:", youngest_age, "| Oldest age level:", oldest_age, "\n")

# --- SINGLE CONTRAST --------------------------------------------------------
# Only ONE age pair is analyzed: oldest vs youngest by default. Change this
# to any 2 values from ordered_age_levels if you want a different pair.
contrast_age_pair <- c(youngest_age, oldest_age)  # c(younger, older)
stopifnot(
  "contrast_age_pair must have exactly 2 elements" = length(contrast_age_pair) == 2,
  "contrast_age_pair values must be in ordered_age_levels" =
    all(contrast_age_pair %in% ordered_age_levels)
)

younger <- contrast_age_pair[1]
older   <- contrast_age_pair[2]

contrast_tbl <- tibble(
  contrast = paste0(older, "-", younger),
  group    = older
)

contrasts_oi <- paste0(
  "'", paste(contrast_tbl$contrast, collapse = "','"), "'"
)

cat("\nSingle contrast analyzed (contrasts_oi):\n"); print(contrasts_oi)
cat("\ncontrast_tbl:\n"); print(contrast_tbl)

```

`sample_id` has the same problem: values such as `"18-F-50"` start with a digit and contain hyphens, which are also invalid for `make.names()`. The original label is kept as a separate column for traceability.

```{r mnn-fix-sample-id}
# Original sample_id looks like "18-F-50": starts with a digit and has
# hyphens -> invalid for make.names(). Keep the original and create a
# valid version to use in the analysis.

colData(sce)$sample_id_original <- colData(sce)$sample_id
colData(sce)$sample_id <- make.names(colData(sce)$sample_id)

cat("Example mapping original sample_id -> valid sample_id:\n")
print(head(unique(data.frame(
  original = colData(sce)$sample_id_original,
  valid    = colData(sce)$sample_id
))))

stopifnot(all(make.names(colData(sce)$sample_id) == colData(sce)$sample_id))
stopifnot(length(unique(colData(sce)$sample_id_original)) == length(unique(colData(sce)$sample_id)))
cat("\nNumber of unique sample_id values:", length(unique(colData(sce)$sample_id)), "\n")


colData(sce)$mouse_id_original <- colData(sce)$mouse.id
colData(sce)$mouse.id <- make.names(colData(sce)$mouse.id)


stopifnot(all(make.names(colData(sce)$mouse.id) == colData(sce)$mouse.id))
stopifnot(length(unique(colData(sce)$mouse_id_original)) == length(unique(colData(sce)$mouse.id)))
cat("\nNumber of unique sample_id values:", length(unique(colData(sce)$mouse.id)), "\n")
```

## Step 2: Load the NicheNet prior model (ligand-receptor + ligand-target + signaling, mouse)

Beyond `lr_network` and `ligand_target_matrix` (already used for prioritization and hub-gene ligand activity), two more prior-model objects are loaded here: `weighted_networks` (ligand-receptor + signaling + TF-target confidence, needed for the receptor heatmap and the signaling-path inference below) and `ligand_tf_matrix` (ligand-to-TF regulatory potential, needed only for signaling-path inference). Both are the mouse versions from the same NicheNet v2 Zenodo record used for `lr_network`/`ligand_target_matrix`.

```{r mnn-prior-model}
options(timeout = 300)

lr_network <- readRDS("nichenet_prior/lr_network_mouse_21122021.rds"
) %>%
  dplyr::rename(ligand = from, receptor = to) %>%
  distinct(ligand, receptor)

ligand_target_matrix <- readRDS(
  "nichenet_prior/ligand_target_matrix_nsga2r_final_mouse.rds"
)

# Needed for: (1) the ligand-receptor heatmap (Step 10-style), and
# (2) signaling-path inference (Step 13-style), both added below.
weighted_networks <- readRDS(
  "nichenet_prior/weighted_networks_nsga2r_final_mouse.rds"
)

# Needed only for signaling-path inference (ligand -> TF -> target).
ligand_tf_matrix <- readRDS(
  "nichenet_prior/ligand_tf_matrix_nsga2r_final_mouse.rds"
)

cat("LR network:", nrow(lr_network), "ligand-receptor pairs\n")
cat("Ligand-target matrix:", dim(ligand_target_matrix)[1], "targets x",
    dim(ligand_target_matrix)[2], "ligands\n")
cat("Weighted networks: lr_sig =", nrow(weighted_networks$lr_sig), "edges | gr =",
    nrow(weighted_networks$gr), "edges\n")
cat("Ligand-TF matrix:", dim(ligand_tf_matrix)[1], "TFs x",
    dim(ligand_tf_matrix)[2], "ligands\n")
```

## Steps 3-6: pseudobulk + per-celltype DE, ligand activity and prioritization

`multi_nichenet_analysis()` is the wrapper that chains steps 3 to 6 of the classic workflow (pseudobulk/abundance calculation per cell type, DE per cell type via muscat/edgeR, ligand activity analysis with the prior model, and the multi-criteria prioritization table). `min_cells` requires a minimum number of cells per sample x celltype combination for that combination to enter the analysis -- adjust if some age groups have few replicates per cell type.

**Design note on `batches`/`covariates`:** `sex` and `tech` (FACS vs. droplet) were both considered as covariate/batch terms, but checking `table(colData(sce)$age, colData(sce)$tech)` and `table(colData(sce)$age, colData(sce)$sex)` showed that in this dataset both variables are almost completely confounded with `age` (e.g. `age1m`, `age18m`, `age21m`, `age30m` are each represented by a single technique, and `age1m`/`age21m`/`age24m`/`age30m` are each represented by a single sex). Because of this, the model cannot separate an age effect from a sex/technique effect for most contrasts, so both are left out (`batches = NA`, `covariates = NA`) and this is documented here as a known limitation of the Tabula Muris Senis sampling design rather than a modeling choice.

```{r mnn-run-analysis}

multinichenet_output <- multi_nichenet_analysis(
  sce                   = sce,
  celltype_id           = "final_celltype",
  sample_id             = "sample_id",
  group_id              = "age",
  batches               = NA,
  covariates            = NA,
  lr_network            = lr_network,
  ligand_target_matrix  = ligand_target_matrix,
  contrasts_oi          = contrasts_oi,
  contrast_tbl          = contrast_tbl,
  min_cells             = 3,
  logFC_threshold       = 0.50,
  p_val_threshold       = 0.05,
  fraction_cutoff       = 0.05,
  p_val_adj             = FALSE,
  empirical_pval        = FALSE,
  top_n_target          = 250,
  verbose               = TRUE
)

saveRDS(multinichenet_output, "multinichenet_output_age.rds")
cat("Total LR pairs in the prioritization table:",
    nrow(multinichenet_output$prioritization_tables$group_prioritization_tbl), "\n")
```

```{r}
multinichenet_output<-readRDS("multinichenet_output_age.rds")
```

### Which cell types were excluded from DE, and why

`multi_nichenet_analysis()` silently drops any cell type that does not have at least 2 samples per group passing `min_cells` (it prints this to the console log, but does not return it as a structured object). This chunk reconstructs that same table directly from `colData(sce)`, so it is available for inspection without having to scroll back through the log.

```{r mnn-check-excluded-celltypes}
included_celltypes <- tryCatch(
  unique(multinichenet_output$celltype_info$sender_receiver_info$sender),
  error = function(e) character(0)
)
if (length(included_celltypes) == 0) {
  # Fallback across multinichenetr versions where the info object is structured differently
  included_celltypes <- tryCatch(
    unique(multinichenet_output$prioritization_tables$group_prioritization_tbl$sender),
    error = function(e) character(0)
  )
}

samples_passing_min_cells <- as.data.frame(colData(sce)) %>%
  count(age, final_celltype, sample_id, name = "n_cells") %>%
  filter(n_cells >= 10) %>%  # keep in sync with min_cells above
  count(age, final_celltype, name = "n_samples_passing")

celltype_status <- samples_passing_min_cells %>%
  group_by(final_celltype) %>%
  summarise(
    n_age_groups_with_2plus_samples = sum(n_samples_passing >= 2),
    n_age_groups_total              = n_distinct(age),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    likely_included = final_celltype %in% included_celltypes,
    fully_covered    = n_age_groups_with_2plus_samples == n_age_groups_total
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_age_groups_with_2plus_samples))

cat("Cell type coverage after the min_samples_per_group / min_cells filters:\n")
print(celltype_status)

cat("\nCell types confirmed present in multinichenet_output:",
    paste(included_celltypes, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

From here on, `multinichenet_output`, `lr_network` and `ligand_target_matrix` are available for the two WGCNA integration sections below.

### QC: cell/sample abundance diagnostics (exported to PDF)

Sanity check before trusting the prioritization results: how many cells per sample x celltype combination actually passed `min_cells`, and how balanced is that across age groups. `multi_nichenet_analysis()` already computes this internally in `abundance_expression_info`; we reuse its built-in plot when available and fall back to a manual count table otherwise (useful given the tech/sex imbalance documented above).

```{r mnn-qc-abundance, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
abund_info <- multinichenet_output$abundance_expression_info

p_abundance <- tryCatch(
  abund_info$abund_plot_sample,
  error = function(e) NULL
)

if (is.null(p_abundance)) {
  # Fallback: build the same kind of diagnostic manually from colData(sce)
  abundance_manual <- as.data.frame(colData(sce)) %>%
    count(sample_id, final_celltype, age, name = "n_cells")

  p_abundance <- ggplot(abundance_manual, aes(x = sample_id, y = n_cells, fill = age)) +
    geom_col() +
    facet_wrap(~ final_celltype, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(title = "Cells per sample x celltype", x = "Sample", y = "N cells") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 6))
}

print(p_abundance)
ggsave("plot_QC_abundance_per_sample_celltype.pdf", p_abundance, width = 9, height = 6)
```

### Circos plot and LR dotplot for the oldest-vs-youngest contrast

Two of MultiNicheNet's signature plots for a single contrast: a circos diagram of sender -\> receiver communication, and a dotplot combining expression, ligand activity and logFC for the top LR pairs. Function names below follow the standard multinichenetr API; if your installed package version differs, run `ls("package:multinichenetr")` and adjust the function names accordingly -- these plotting helpers have changed across versions.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(circlize)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(grid)
library(gridExtra)
library(magick)  # para rasterizar los PDFs individuales

graphics.off()

# ==============================================================================
# 1. REORDER AGES IN MULTINICHENET (age3m AT THE START)
# ==============================================================================
age_order <- ordered_age_levels  # dynamic (was hardcoded to a fixed set of 5 age strings)

multinichenet_output$prioritization_tables <- lapply(
  multinichenet_output$prioritization_tables, function(tbl) {
    if (is.data.frame(tbl) && "group" %in% colnames(tbl)) {
      tbl$group <- factor(tbl$group, levels = age_order)
    }
    return(tbl)
  }
)

if (!is.null(multinichenet_output$celltype_info$sample_id_info)) {
  if ("group" %in% colnames(multinichenet_output$celltype_info$sample_id_info)) {
    multinichenet_output$celltype_info$sample_id_info$group <- factor(
      multinichenet_output$celltype_info$sample_id_info$group, 
      levels = age_order
    )
  }
}

# ==============================================================================
# 2. EXTRACT TOP L-R PAIRS FOR CONTRAST
# ==============================================================================
contrast_oi <- paste0(oldest_age, "-", youngest_age)

get_lr_pairs_for_contrast <- function(contrast_str, top_n = 50) {
  tbl <- multinichenet_output$prioritization_tables$group_prioritization_tbl
  stopifnot("contrast" %in% colnames(tbl))
  
  rank_col <- intersect(c("prioritization_score", "prioritization_rank"), colnames(tbl))
  tbl_contrast <- tbl %>% dplyr::filter(contrast == contrast_str)
  
  if (length(rank_col) > 0) {
    tbl_contrast <- tbl_contrast %>% 
      dplyr::arrange(if (rank_col[1] == "prioritization_rank") prioritization_rank else desc(.data[[rank_col[1]]]))
  }
  
  tbl_contrast %>% 
    dplyr::distinct(sender, receiver, ligand, receptor, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
    dplyr::slice_head(n = top_n)
}

lr_prioritized_50 <- get_lr_pairs_for_contrast(contrast_oi, top_n = 50)

cat("Interactions retrieved for '", contrast_oi, "': ", nrow(lr_prioritized_50), "\n")

# ==============================================================================
# 3. UNIFIED CELL-TYPE COLOR PALETTE
# ==============================================================================
all_senders   <- unique(lr_prioritized_50$sender)
all_receivers <- unique(lr_prioritized_50$receiver)
all_celltypes <- unique(c(all_senders, all_receivers))

palette_colors <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(max(3, length(all_celltypes)), "Set2")[1:length(all_celltypes)]
names(palette_colors) <- all_celltypes

colors_sender_vec   <- palette_colors[all_senders]
colors_receiver_vec <- palette_colors[all_receivers]

# ==============================================================================
# 4. SPLIT TOP 50 INTO 3 CHUNKS
# ==============================================================================
n_total    <- nrow(lr_prioritized_50)
n_chunks   <- 3
chunk_size <- ceiling(n_total / n_chunks)

circos_part_list <- list()
for (i in 1:n_chunks) {
  start_idx <- (i - 1) * chunk_size + 1
  end_idx   <- min(i * chunk_size, n_total)
  
  if (start_idx <= n_total) {
    tbl_i <- lr_prioritized_50 %>% 
      dplyr::slice(start_idx:end_idx) %>% 
      dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("weight", "weight.x", "weight.y")))
    colnames(tbl_i) <- make.unique(colnames(tbl_i))
    circos_part_list[[paste0("part", i)]] <- tbl_i
  }
}

# ==============================================================================
# 5. RENDERIZAR CADA CÍRCULO EN SU PROPIO PDF (método que YA sabemos que funciona)
# ==============================================================================
cat("\n--- Rendering individual circos plots (as single-page PDFs) ---\n")

tmp_dir   <- tempdir()
pdf_paths <- c()

for (i in seq_along(circos_part_list)) {
  
  part_name <- names(circos_part_list)[i]
  tbl_i     <- circos_part_list[[part_name]]
  pdf_path  <- file.path(tmp_dir, paste0("circos_", part_name, ".pdf"))
  
  pdf(pdf_path, width = 8, height = 8)
  
  result <- tryCatch({
    par(mar = c(3, 3, 4, 3))
    circlize::circos.clear()
    
    make_circos_group_comparison(
      prioritized_tbl_oi = tbl_i,
      colors_sender       = colors_sender_vec,
      colors_receiver     = colors_receiver_vec
    )
    
    title(
      main = paste0("Part ", i, " [", nrow(tbl_i), " pairs]"),
      line = 1,
      cex.main = 1.6,
      font.main = 2
    )
    
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("ERROR en ", part_name, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
    FALSE
  })
  
  dev.off()
  
  if (isTRUE(result)) {
    cat(part_name, "renderizado correctamente (", nrow(tbl_i), "pares )\n")
    pdf_paths <- c(pdf_paths, pdf_path)
  } else {
    cat(part_name, "NO se pudo renderizar — revisa el error de arriba\n")
  }
}

# ==============================================================================
# 6. RASTERIZAR CADA PDF INDIVIDUAL A IMAGEN DE ALTA RESOLUCIÓN (con magick)
# ==============================================================================
cat("\n--- Converting individual PDFs to high-res images ---\n")

circle_grobs <- lapply(pdf_paths, function(p) {
  img <- magick::image_read_pdf(p, density = 300)
  grid::rasterGrob(as.raster(img), interpolate = TRUE)
})

# ==============================================================================
# 7. RENDERIZAR LA LEYENDA (una sola vez) COMO SU PROPIO PDF -> IMAGEN
# ==============================================================================
legend_pdf_path <- file.path(tmp_dir, "circos_legend.pdf")

pdf(legend_pdf_path, width = 2.5, height = 8)
par(mar = c(1, 1, 1, 1))
plot.new()
legend(
  "center",
  legend = names(palette_colors),
  fill = palette_colors,
  border = NA,
  bty = "n",
  title = "Cell Types",
  title.font = 2,
  cex = 1.3,
  y.intersp = 1.6
)
dev.off()

legend_img  <- magick::image_read_pdf(legend_pdf_path, density = 300)
legend_grob <- grid::rasterGrob(as.raster(legend_img), interpolate = TRUE)

# ==============================================================================
# 8. ENSAMBLAR: CÍRCULOS EN ORDEN A LA IZQUIERDA + LEYENDA UNA SOLA VEZ A LA DERECHA
# ==============================================================================
cat("\n--- Assembling final single-page PDF ---\n")

circos_pdf_filename <- "plot_circos_3panels_top50.pdf"

if (length(circle_grobs) == 0) {
  stop("Ningún círculo se renderizó correctamente. Revisa los mensajes de error de arriba antes de continuar.")
}

pdf(circos_pdf_filename, width = 24, height = 7.5)

grid.arrange(
  grobs = c(circle_grobs, list(legend_grob)),
  ncol  = length(circle_grobs) + 1,
  widths = c(rep(3, length(circle_grobs)), 1),
  top = grid::textGrob(
    paste0("Top L-R Interactions (", contrast_oi, ")"),
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 16, fontface = "bold")
  )
)

dev.off()



# ==============================================================================
# 9. LR DOTPLOTS (TOP 50 SPLIT INTO 3 PARTS) — SIN CAMBIOS
# ==============================================================================
cat("\n--- Generating LR Dotplots (Top 50 split into 3 parts) ---\n")

for (part_name in names(circos_part_list)) {
  i <- as.integer(sub("part", "", part_name))
  start_idx <- (i - 1) * chunk_size + 1
  end_idx   <- min(i * chunk_size, n_total)
  tbl_sub   <- lr_prioritized_50 %>% dplyr::slice(start_idx:end_idx)
  
  p_sub <- tryCatch(
    make_sample_lr_prod_activity_plots(
      prioritization_tables = multinichenet_output$prioritization_tables,
      prioritized_tbl_oi    = tbl_sub
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      message(" Error in Dotplot of ", part_name, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
      NULL
    }
  )
  
  if (!is.null(p_sub)) {
    p_sub_wide <- p_sub & 
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6.5, angle = 45, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5),
        strip.text  = element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold"),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 35, r = 15, b = 15, l = 15, unit = "pt")
      )
    
    dotplot_pdf_name <- paste0("plot_LR_dotplot_", part_name, "_ultra_wide.pdf")
    ggsave(dotplot_pdf_name, p_sub_wide, width = 22, height = 13, limitsize = FALSE)
    cat("LR Dotplot saved as:", dotplot_pdf_name, "\n")
  }
}

```

## Validation: overlap between age-associated WGCNA modules and MultiNicheNet prioritization

Idea: if a ligand or receptor prioritized by MultiNicheNet as relevant for the age contrast **also** falls inside a WGCNA module that the independent WGCNA analysis already flagged as age-associated -- and, moreover, in the **same cell type** (sender for the ligand, receiver for the receptor) -- that is cross-method evidence from two approaches that start from different information (co-expression topology vs. ligand-receptor prior model + DE).

```{r}

# ============================================================
# 0. NUEVO -- combinar correlación lineal (significant_modules)
#    y trayectoria (significant_trajectory_modules) en un solo
#    criterio de "módulo asociado a edad". Va ANTES de todo lo
#    demás que dependa de significant_modules.
# ============================================================
age_association_summary <- module_trait_table %>%
  dplyr::select(module, correlation, p_value_corr = p_value, fdr_corr = fdr) %>%
  full_join(
    module_trajectory %>%
      dplyr::select(module, shape, category, p_value_traj = p_value,
                    fdr_traj = fdr, r_squared),
    by = "module"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sig_correlation = !is.na(fdr_corr) & fdr_corr < 0.05,
    sig_trajectory  = !is.na(fdr_traj) & fdr_traj < 0.05,
    age_associated  = sig_correlation | sig_trajectory
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(age_associated), fdr_corr, fdr_traj)

age_associated_modules <- age_association_summary %>%
  filter(age_associated) %>%
  pull(module)

cat("Módulos asociados a edad (correlación lineal y/o trayectoria):",
    length(age_associated_modules), "\n")
print(age_association_summary %>% filter(age_associated) %>%
        dplyr::select(module, correlation, fdr_corr, shape, category, fdr_traj))

```

```{r multinichenet-validation-setup}

# Same fix as the circos/dotplot section above: filter by the exact
# `contrast` string, not by the pooled `group` label, which would otherwise
# mix several different age comparisons together.
age_group_oi <- oldest_age  # kept for readable labels/titles below

# Target the single contrast defined in Step 1 (dynamic, not hardcoded --
# with contrast_tbl now holding exactly one row, this is that one contrast).
contrast_oi <- contrast_tbl$contrast[1]

lr_prioritized <- multinichenet_output$prioritization_tables$group_prioritization_tbl %>% dplyr::filter(contrast == contrast_oi) %>% dplyr::slice_max(order_by = prioritization_score, n = 250)
```

```{r multinichenet-validation-crossref}

# ============================================================
module_ct_lookup <- gene_celltype_module %>%
  filter(module %in% age_associated_modules) %>%   # antes: significant_modules
  distinct(module, celltype, gene)

lr_prioritized_annotated <- lr_prioritized %>%
  left_join(
    module_ct_lookup %>% rename(ligand = gene, sender = celltype, ligand_module = module),
    by = c("ligand", "sender")
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    module_ct_lookup %>% rename(receptor = gene, receiver = celltype, receptor_module = module),
    by = c("receptor", "receiver")
  )

overlap_summary <- lr_prioritized_annotated %>%
  summarise(
    n_total_pairs            = n(),
    n_ligand_in_age_module   = sum(!is.na(ligand_module)),
    n_receptor_in_age_module = sum(!is.na(receptor_module)),
    n_both_in_age_module     = sum(!is.na(ligand_module) & !is.na(receptor_module))
  )

cat("Overlap summary (age-prioritized LR pairs vs. age-associated WGCNA modules):\n")
print(overlap_summary)
write.csv(lr_prioritized_annotated, "multinichenet_age_LR_wgcna_overlap.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

### Is the overlap greater than expected by chance?

Global hypergeometric test: of all ligand/receptor genes prioritized by MultiNicheNet for the age contrast (that were also part of the tested universe in WGCNA), how many fall in an age-associated module, compared to the proportion expected under random assignment?

```{r multinichenet-validation-hypergeom}

age_module_genes <- gene_celltype_module %>%
  filter(module %in% age_associated_modules) %>%   # antes: significant_modules
  distinct(gene) %>%
  pull(gene)

lr_genes_tested <- unique(c(lr_prioritized$ligand, lr_prioritized$receptor))
lr_genes_tested <- intersect(lr_genes_tested, universe_symbols)

n_overlap  <- length(intersect(lr_genes_tested, age_module_genes))
n_age_mod  <- length(intersect(age_module_genes, universe_symbols))
n_universe <- length(universe_symbols)
n_lr       <- length(lr_genes_tested)

p_enrich <- phyper(n_overlap - 1, n_age_mod, n_universe - n_age_mod, n_lr, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("MultiNicheNet ligand/receptor genes also present in the WGCNA network:", n_lr, "\n")
cat("From which,", n_overlap, "fall into a WGCNA module asociated with age \n")
cat("Hipergeometric enrichment, p =", signif(p_enrich, 3), "\n")
```

```{r multinichenet-validation-plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}

plot_data <- bind_rows(
  lr_prioritized_annotated %>% filter(!is.na(ligand_module)) %>%
    transmute(module = ligand_module, role = "Ligand"),
  lr_prioritized_annotated %>% filter(!is.na(receptor_module)) %>%
    transmute(module = receptor_module, role = "Receptor")
)

p_validation <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = module, fill = role)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "WGCNA module (age-associated)", y = "Number of prioritized LR pairs",
       title = "MultiNicheNet LR pairs falling in age-associated WGCNA modules",
       subtitle = paste0("Contrast: ", age_group_oi, " | global hypergeometric p = ", signif(p_enrich, 3))) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

print(p_validation)

ggsave("plot_LR_wgcna_module_overlap.pdf", p_validation, width = 7, height = 5)
```

### Validation across contrasts (generic, works for 1..N contrasts)

The spotlight above covered the single contrast defined in Step 1 (`r contrast_oi`). The same overlap + hypergeometric logic is generalized here and applied to **every contrast in `contrast_tbl$contrast`** -- iterating over `contrast`, not the pooled `group` label, since a single age level can be the "group" of several different comparisons at once (see the note in the circos/dotplot section above). With the pipeline now restricted to a single age contrast (Step 1), this loop runs over exactly that one contrast and reproduces the spotlight result above; the code is kept generic (rather than hardcoded to one contrast) so it keeps working unchanged if you ever add more rows to `contrast_tbl`.

```{r}


# 1. Función para extraer los pares usando prioritization_tables
get_lr_pairs_for_contrast <- function(contrast_str, multinichenet_res, top_n = 250) {
  
  # Acceso directo a prioritization_tables (estructura estándar de MultiNicheNet)
  # Si prioritization_tables es una lista de tablas, toma group_prioritization_tbl;
  # si es el data frame directo, lo asigna.
  prior_tbl <- if (is.data.frame(multinichenet_res$prioritization_tables)) {
    multinichenet_res$prioritization_tables
  } else if (!is.null(multinichenet_res$prioritization_tables$group_prioritization_tbl)) {
    multinichenet_res$prioritization_tables$group_prioritization_tbl
  } else {
    NULL
  }
  
  if (is.null(prior_tbl)) {
    warning(paste("No se encontró la tabla de priorización para el contraste:", contrast_str))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Detectar automáticamente si la columna se llama prioritization_score o score
  score_col <- if ("prioritization_score" %in% colnames(prior_tbl)) {
    "prioritization_score"
  } else if ("score" %in% colnames(prior_tbl)) {
    "score"
  } else {
    colnames(prior_tbl)[grep("score|rank", colnames(prior_tbl))[1]]
  }
  
  # Filtrar los top N pares por contraste
  lr_top <- prior_tbl %>%
    filter(contrast == contrast_str) %>%
    slice_max(order_by = .data[[score_col]], n = top_n, with_ties = FALSE)
  
  return(lr_top)
}

# 2. Función de validación por contraste
run_validation_for_contrast <- function(contrast_str, multinichenet_res) {
  
  lr_oi <- get_lr_pairs_for_contrast(
    contrast_str = contrast_str, 
    multinichenet_res = multinichenet_res, 
    top_n = 250
  )
  
  # Retornar tibble estructurado si no hay datos
  if (is.null(lr_oi) || nrow(lr_oi) == 0) {
    return(tibble(
      contrast                 = contrast_str,
      n_total_pairs            = 0,
      n_ligand_in_age_module   = 0,
      n_receptor_in_age_module = 0,
      n_lr_genes_tested        = 0,
      n_lr_genes_in_age_module = 0,
      p_hypergeometric         = NA_real_
    ))
  }
  
  # Anotación con los módulos por celda/gen
  lr_oi_annotated <- lr_oi %>%
    left_join(
      module_ct_lookup %>% rename(ligand = gene, sender = celltype, ligand_module = module),
      by = c("ligand", "sender")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      module_ct_lookup %>% rename(receptor = gene, receiver = celltype, receptor_module = module),
      by = c("receptor", "receiver")
    )
  
  # Genes únicos involucrados en las interacciones
  lr_genes_oi <- unique(c(lr_oi$ligand, lr_oi$receptor))
  lr_genes_oi <- intersect(lr_genes_oi, universe_symbols)
  
  n_overlap_oi <- length(intersect(lr_genes_oi, age_module_genes))
  n_lr_oi      <- length(lr_genes_oi)
  
  # Test hipergeométrico
  p_oi <- if (n_lr_oi > 0) {
    phyper(n_overlap_oi - 1, n_age_mod, n_universe - n_age_mod, n_lr_oi, lower.tail = FALSE)
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }
  
  tibble(
    contrast                 = contrast_str,
    n_total_pairs            = nrow(lr_oi),
    n_ligand_in_age_module   = sum(!is.na(lr_oi_annotated$ligand_module)),
    n_receptor_in_age_module = sum(!is.na(lr_oi_annotated$receptor_module)),
    n_lr_genes_tested        = n_lr_oi,
    n_lr_genes_in_age_module = n_overlap_oi,
    p_hypergeometric         = p_oi
  )
}

# 3. Ejecución corregida sobre todos los contrastes
validation_all_contrasts <- purrr::map_dfr(
  unique(contrast_tbl$contrast), 
  ~ run_validation_for_contrast(.x, multinichenet_res = multinichenet_output)
) %>%
  mutate(
    fdr_hypergeometric = if (all(is.na(p_hypergeometric))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      p.adjust(p_hypergeometric, method = "BH")
    }
  ) %>%
  arrange(p_hypergeometric)
```

### GO enrichment of the LR / age-module overlap gene set (reused from WGCNA_24)

No new enrichment is run here. `WGCNA_24.Rmd` already computed GO Biological Process enrichment per module -- `go_full_module_df` (all module genes) and `go_hubs_df` (hub genes only), both already restricted to `pvalueCutoff = 0.05` and BH-adjusted -- and both objects are still in the environment from that earlier run. This section just **filters** those precomputed results down to the terms whose gene set (`geneID`, slash-separated gene symbols since `readable = TRUE` was used) overlaps with the genes that are *both* LR-prioritized by MultiNicheNet *and* already in an age-associated module (`overlap_genes`, same definition as the hypergeometric test above), restricted to `significant_modules`.

```{r}

library(tidyverse)

# Resolver conflictos de nombres entre tidyverse y paquetes tipo Bioconductor/lubridate
if (requireNamespace("conflicted", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(conflicted)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::select, .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter, .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::mutate, .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::arrange, .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(base::intersect, .quiet = TRUE)
}

overlap_genes <- lr_genes_tested[lr_genes_tested %in% age_module_genes]
cat("Genes entrando al filtro GO (LR-priorizados Y en un módulo asociado a edad):",
    length(overlap_genes), "\n")

filter_precomputed_go <- function(go_df, source_label) {
  if (is.null(go_df) || nrow(go_df) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  go_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(module %in% age_associated_modules) %>%   
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(geneID) & geneID != "") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      # str_split devuelve una lista directamente sin requerir índices numéricos arriesgados
      current_genes     = stringr::str_split(as.character(geneID), "/"),
      intersect_genes   = purrr::map(current_genes, ~ base::intersect(.x, overlap_genes)),
      n_overlap_genes   = purrr::map_int(intersect_genes, length),
      overlap_hit_genes = purrr::map_chr(intersect_genes, ~ paste(.x, collapse = "/"))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(n_overlap_genes > 0) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(go_source = source_label) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(p.adjust) %>%
    dplyr::select(-current_genes, -intersect_genes)
}

go_overlap_full <- filter_precomputed_go(go_bp_by_module_celltype, "GO_BP (todos los genes del módulo)")

hub_lookup <- hub_genes_table %>% dplyr::distinct(module, celltype, gene)

go_overlap_hubs <- go_overlap_full %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Aplicamos la misma lógica segura con stringr para evitar subíndices fuera de límites
    split_hits    = stringr::str_split(ifelse(is.na(overlap_hit_genes), "", overlap_hit_genes), "/"),
    target_hubs   = purrr::map2(module, celltype, ~ hub_lookup$gene[hub_lookup$module == .x & hub_lookup$celltype == .y]),
    intersect_hub = purrr::map2(split_hits, target_hubs, base::intersect),
    hub_hit_genes = purrr::map_chr(intersect_hub, ~ paste(.x, collapse = "/"))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(hub_hit_genes != "") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(go_source = "GO_BP (subset con hub genes)") %>%
  dplyr::select(-split_hits, -target_hubs, -intersect_hub)

go_overlap_combined <- dplyr::bind_rows(go_overlap_hubs, go_overlap_full)

cat("Términos GO BP (de WGCNA_24) que tocan el set de solape LR/módulo:",
    nrow(go_overlap_combined), "\n")

write.csv(go_overlap_combined, "GO_LR_wgcna_overlap_from_precomputed.csv", row.names = FALSE)

go_enrich_plot <- NULL
if (!is.null(go_overlap_combined) && nrow(go_overlap_combined) > 0) {
  
  go_overlap_top <- go_overlap_combined %>%
    dplyr::group_by(go_source) %>%
    dplyr::slice_min(p.adjust, n = 15, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      # Etiqueta más corta y envuelta en varias líneas para que no aplaste el panel
      label = stringr::str_wrap(paste(Description, celltype, sep = " | "), width = 45)
    )
  
  cat("Distribución de términos por go_source:\n")
  print(table(go_overlap_top$go_source))
  
  go_enrich_plot <- ggplot(
    go_overlap_top,
    aes(x = reorder(label, -p.adjust),
        y = -log10(p.adjust), size = n_overlap_genes, color = module)
  ) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
    coord_flip() +
    facet_wrap(~ go_source, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 7)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "-log10(p.adjust)",
         color = "Módulo", size = "N genes solapados",
         title = "Términos GO (BP) de WGCNA_24 que tocan el set de solape LR/WGCNA",
         subtitle = "Enrichment reutilizado tal cual de WGCNA_24.Rmd -- no recalculado aquí") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, margin = margin(b = 4)),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, color = "gray40", margin = margin(b = 10)),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5, lineheight = 0.85),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
      legend.position = "right",
      plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 15, b = 10, l = 10)
    )
  
  print(go_enrich_plot)
  
  # Alto dinámico según número de términos y facetas, para que no se aplasten
  n_terms     <- nrow(go_overlap_top)
  n_sources   <- dplyr::n_distinct(go_overlap_top$go_source)
  plot_height <- max(6, n_terms / n_sources * 0.35 * n_sources)
  
  ggsave("plot_GO_LR_wgcna_overlap_from_precomputed.pdf",
         go_enrich_plot, width = 11, height = plot_height, limitsize = FALSE)
  
} else {
  cat("Ninguno de los términos GO BP precomputados (WGCNA_24) contiene un gen del set de solape LR/módulo.\n")
}
```

```{r}
  dplyr::count(module, celltype, name = "n_hub_genes") %>%

top_hit <- switch(
```
