```{r}
  fdr_corr        = module_celltype_candidates %>% dplyr::filter(sig_correlation) %>% dplyr::slice_min(fdr_corr, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE),
  abs_correlation = module_celltype_candidates %>% dplyr::filter(sig_correlation) %>% dplyr::slice_max(abs_correlation, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE),
  fdr_traj        = module_celltype_candidates %>% dplyr::filter(sig_trajectory) %>% dplyr::slice_min(fdr_traj, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE),
  r_squared       = module_celltype_candidates %>% dplyr::filter(sig_trajectory) %>% dplyr::slice_max(r_squared, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE),
  stop("SELECTION_METRIC debe ser 'fdr_corr', 'abs_correlation', 'fdr_traj' o 'r_squared'")
)

module_oi   <- top_hit$module
receiver_oi <- top_hit$celltype
```

## Mechanistic hypothesis: age-associated module hub genes as the target gene set

Instead of using MultiNicheNet's standard DE genes as the gene set of interest in the ligand activity analysis, here we use the **hub genes** (top kME) of a specific module, restricted to the cell type where that module's genes originate. This directly asks: *which ligands, from which candidate cell types, could be driving the co-expression program that WGCNA found in this cell type?* This whole section follows the classic NicheNet receiver-centric logic (Steps 2-3, 5-11, 13 of the [ngs101.com NicheNet tutorial](https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-10-cell-cell-communication-analysis-using-nichenet/)), adapted so the receiver, the gene set of interest, and the receiver/sender cell types all come from WGCNA rather than from a fresh DE test.

Note on `module_oi`/`receiver_oi` selection: WGCNA's modules are built from a **single combined network** of `gene_celltype` features (all `target_celltypes` mixed together), so a module-age correlation (`module_trait_table`) exists only **per module**, not per (module, celltype) -- there is no separate age-correlation value for "this module in Fibroblasts" vs. "this module in Myocytes". What legitimately varies by cell type is *which* cell types actually contributed hub genes to a given significant module (`hub_genes_table$celltype`). `module_celltype_candidates` below combines both pieces of information correctly: the module-level FDR/correlation from `module_trait_table`, crossed with every (module, celltype) combination that actually has hub genes, restricted to `target_celltypes` (so senders/receiver both stay within the same 4 cell types WGCNA and MultiNicheNet were restricted to).

### Step 3 (WGCNA-adapted): real expressed genes per cell type

The previous version of this section used `gene_celltype_module$gene` (the \~20K WGCNA age-dispersion HVGs) as a stand-in for "genes expressed in this cell type", for both the background gene universe and the sender ligand pool. That is too narrow: those \~20K genes are the ones WGCNA *selected* as highly age-variable, not the full set of genes actually expressed in each cell type, and using them as the ligand-activity background biases the corrected AUPR statistic (a smaller, non-random background changes what "enriched relative to background" means). Following Step 3 of the NicheNet tutorial, real expressed genes are computed here with `nichenetr::get_expressed_genes()` (\>= 10% of a cell type's cells, the same convention the tutorial uses) directly on `seurat_mnn` -- the exact same cells/cell types WGCNA and MultiNicheNet both use. WGCNA's gene set (`gene_celltype_module`) is still used for what it's actually meant for: defining `geneset_oi`, the hub genes themselves.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Resolver conflictos de nombres entre tidyverse y otros paquetes cargados
if (requireNamespace("conflicted", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(conflicted)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::select, .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter, .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::mutate, .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::arrange, .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::count, .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(base::intersect, .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(base::union, .quiet = TRUE)
}

EXPRESSION_PCT <- 0.10  # same convention as the NicheNet tutorial (>=10% of cells)

expr_mat_mnn    <- Seurat::GetAssayData(seurat_mnn, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
cell_idents_mnn <- seurat_mnn$final_celltype

expressed_genes_by_celltype <- setNames(
  lapply(target_celltypes, function(ct) {
    nichenetr::get_expressed_genes(
      celltype_oi    = ct,
      object         = expr_mat_mnn,
      celltype_annot = cell_idents_mnn,
      pct            = EXPRESSION_PCT
    )
  }),
  target_celltypes
)

cat("Real expressed genes per cell type (>=", EXPRESSION_PCT * 100, "% of cells):\n")
print(vapply(expressed_genes_by_celltype, length, integer(1)))

# Union across all 4 target_celltypes = the real "expressed_genes_sender" pool
# used by the sender-agnostic ligand activity approach further below.
expressed_genes_union <- Reduce(base::union, expressed_genes_by_celltype)
cat("\nUnion of expressed genes across all target_celltypes:", length(expressed_genes_union), "\n")

rm(expr_mat_mnn, cell_idents_mnn)
```

### Setup: module/celltype selection, gene set of interest, real background

```{r hub-genes-ligand-activity-setup}
# Build the (module x celltype) candidate table: module-level significance
# from module_trait_table, crossed with which cell types actually have hub
# genes in that module (from hub_genes_table), restricted to target_celltypes.
module_celltype_candidates <- hub_genes_table %>%
  filter(celltype %in% target_celltypes) %>%
  count(module, celltype, name = "n_hub_genes") %>%
  inner_join(
    module_trait_table %>% dplyr::select(module, correlation, p_value, fdr),
    by = "module"
  ) %>%
  filter(p_value < 0.05) %>%
  mutate(abs_correlation = abs(correlation)) %>%
  arrange(fdr, desc(n_hub_genes))

cat("Significant (module x celltype) candidates (FDR < 0.05, restricted to target_celltypes):\n")
print(module_celltype_candidates)
write.csv(module_celltype_candidates, "module_celltype_candidates.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("Candidatos exportados a module_celltype_candidates.csv\n")

# Which criterion to rank candidates by, before picking the top one:
#  - "fdr"              : most statistically confident module-age association (default)
#  - "abs_correlation"   : strongest module-age effect size, regardless of FDR rank
SELECTION_METRIC <- "fdr"  # change to "abs_correlation" to select by effect size instead

top_hit <- switch(
  SELECTION_METRIC,
  fdr             = module_celltype_candidates %>% slice_min(fdr, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE),
  abs_correlation = module_celltype_candidates %>% slice_max(abs_correlation, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE),
  stop("SELECTION_METRIC must be 'fdr' or 'abs_correlation'")
)
# To force a specific module/celltype manually instead, uncomment and edit:
# top_hit <- module_celltype_candidates %>% filter(module == "turquoise", celltype == "Fibroblasts")

module_oi   <- top_hit$module
receiver_oi <- top_hit$celltype

cat("\nSelection metric:", SELECTION_METRIC, "\n")
cat("Module of interest:", module_oi, "| Receiver cell type:", receiver_oi,
    "| Module-age FDR:", signif(top_hit$fdr, 3),
    "| Module-age correlation:", signif(top_hit$correlation, 3), "\n")

# Hub genes of THAT module, selected specifically from THAT cell type
# (the `celltype` column in hub_genes_table = origin celltype of the gene_celltype feature)
geneset_oi <- hub_genes_table %>%
  filter(module == module_oi, celltype == receiver_oi) %>%
  pull(gene) %>%
  unique()

geneset_oi <- geneset_oi[geneset_oi %in% rownames(ligand_target_matrix)]
cat("Hub genes used as the target gene set:", length(geneset_oi), "\n")

# The tutorial recommends 50-500 genes for a stable ligand activity signal;
# with a small module this can easily fall well below that. Warn loudly
# rather than silently reporting an AUPR built on very few genes.
MIN_GENESET_SIZE <- 20
if (length(geneset_oi) < MIN_GENESET_SIZE) {
  warning(
    "geneset_oi has only ", length(geneset_oi), " genes (< ", MIN_GENESET_SIZE,
    "). Ligand activity (AUPR) estimates from this few genes are unstable -- ",
    "consider a larger/less strict module, a lower hub_percentile in WGCNA_24, ",
    "or interpreting the ranking below qualitatively rather than quantitatively."
  )
}

# REAL background: genes actually expressed in the receiver cell type
# (>=10% of its cells, computed above), NOT just the WGCNA-selected HVGs --
# this is the statistically correct background for predict_ligand_activities().
background_expressed_genes <- expressed_genes_by_celltype[[receiver_oi]] %>%
  intersect(rownames(ligand_target_matrix))

cat("Real background expressed genes in", receiver_oi, ":", length(background_expressed_genes), "\n")
cat("(for comparison, WGCNA-HVG-only background would have been:",
    length(intersect(unique(gene_celltype_module$gene[gene_celltype_module$celltype == receiver_oi]),
                      rownames(ligand_target_matrix))), ")\n")
```

### Ligand activity: sender-focused AND sender-agnostic (Step 5-7 style)

Two candidate-ligand definitions are run and compared, as recommended by the NicheNet tutorial: **sender-focused** (ligand expressed in a specific `target_celltypes` sender AND its receptor expressed in the receiver -- iterated per sender cell type, as before) and **sender-agnostic** (any ligand in `lr_network` whose receptor is expressed in the receiver, regardless of which cell type expresses the ligand). Ligands that rank highly in *both* are the strongest candidates; ligands unique to the sender-agnostic list may come from cell types outside `target_celltypes` (i.e. cell types WGCNA/MultiNicheNet excluded) and should be interpreted with that caveat.

```{r}
run_candidate_plots <- function(module_oi, receiver_oi, verbose = TRUE) {
  
  geneset_oi <- hub_genes_table %>%
    dplyr::filter(module == module_oi, celltype == receiver_oi) %>%
    dplyr::pull(gene) %>%
    unique()
  geneset_oi <- geneset_oi[geneset_oi %in% rownames(ligand_target_matrix)]
  
  if (verbose) cat("\n===== Módulo:", module_oi, "| Receptor:", receiver_oi,
                   "| Hub genes:", length(geneset_oi), "=====\n")
  
  if (length(geneset_oi) < MIN_GENESET_SIZE) {
    warning("[", module_oi, "/", receiver_oi, "] geneset_oi tiene solo ", length(geneset_oi),
            " genes (< ", MIN_GENESET_SIZE, "). Las estimaciones de ligand activity (AUPR) ",
            "serán inestables.")
  }
  if (length(geneset_oi) < 5) {
    cat("  -> Se salta", module_oi, "/", receiver_oi, ": geneset_oi demasiado pequeño (<5 genes).\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  result <- tryCatch({
    
    background_expressed_genes <- expressed_genes_by_celltype[[receiver_oi]] %>%
      intersect(rownames(ligand_target_matrix))
    
    sender_celltypes    <- base::setdiff(target_celltypes, receiver_oi)
    expressed_receptors <- base::intersect(lr_network$receptor, background_expressed_genes)
    
    # --- Sender-focused: una corrida de ligand activity POR sender celltype ---
    ligand_activities_by_sender <- purrr::map_dfr(sender_celltypes, function(sender_ct) {
      sender_expressed_genes <- expressed_genes_by_celltype[[sender_ct]]
      expressed_ligands <- base::intersect(lr_network$ligand, sender_expressed_genes)
      
      potential_ligands <- lr_network %>%
        dplyr::filter(ligand %in% expressed_ligands, receptor %in% expressed_receptors) %>%
        dplyr::pull(ligand) %>%
        unique()
      
      if (length(potential_ligands) < 1) return(NULL)
      
      act <- tryCatch(
        nichenetr::predict_ligand_activities(
          geneset                    = geneset_oi,
          background_expressed_genes = background_expressed_genes,
          ligand_target_matrix       = ligand_target_matrix,
          potential_ligands          = potential_ligands
        ),
        error = function(e) {
          message("  [", module_oi, "/", receiver_oi, "] Sender '", sender_ct,
                  "': ligand activity falló (", conditionMessage(e), ")")
          NULL
        }
      )
      if (is.null(act)) return(NULL)
      
      act$sender   <- sender_ct
      act$approach <- "sender-focused"
      act
    })
    
    if (nrow(ligand_activities_by_sender) == 0 || !"aupr_corrected" %in% names(ligand_activities_by_sender)) {
      cat("  -> Ningún sender produjo ligand activities válidas para", module_oi, "/", receiver_oi,
          "-- se salta.\n")
      return(NULL)
    }
    ligand_activities_by_sender <- ligand_activities_by_sender %>%
      dplyr::arrange(desc(aupr_corrected))
    
    # --- Sender-agnostic: UNA corrida, cualquier ligando con receptor expresado en el receptor ---
    potential_ligands_agnostic <- lr_network %>%
      dplyr::filter(ligand %in% expressed_genes_union, receptor %in% expressed_receptors) %>%
      dplyr::pull(ligand) %>%
      unique()
    
    ligand_activities_agnostic <- tryCatch(
      nichenetr::predict_ligand_activities(
        geneset                    = geneset_oi,
        background_expressed_genes = background_expressed_genes,
        ligand_target_matrix       = ligand_target_matrix,
        potential_ligands          = potential_ligands_agnostic
      ),
      error = function(e) {
        message("  [", module_oi, "/", receiver_oi, "] Sender-agnostic ligand activity falló (",
                conditionMessage(e), ")")
        NULL
      }
    )
    if (!is.null(ligand_activities_agnostic)) {
      ligand_activities_agnostic <- ligand_activities_agnostic %>%
        dplyr::arrange(desc(aupr_corrected)) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(sender = NA_character_, approach = "sender-agnostic")
    }
    
    write.csv(
      ligand_activities_by_sender,
      paste0("ligand_activity_hubgenes_", module_oi, "_", receiver_oi, "_sender_focused.csv"),
      row.names = FALSE
    )
    if (!is.null(ligand_activities_agnostic)) {
      write.csv(
        ligand_activities_agnostic,
        paste0("ligand_activity_hubgenes_", module_oi, "_", receiver_oi, "_sender_agnostic.csv"),
        row.names = FALSE
      )
    }
    
    top_ligands_focused_set <- ligand_activities_by_sender %>%
      dplyr::slice_max(aupr_corrected, n = TOP_N_LIGANDS, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
      dplyr::pull(test_ligand) %>% unique()
    
    top_ligands_agnostic_set <- if (!is.null(ligand_activities_agnostic)) {
      ligand_activities_agnostic %>%
        dplyr::slice_max(aupr_corrected, n = TOP_N_LIGANDS, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
        dplyr::pull(test_ligand) %>% unique()
    } else character(0)
    
    best_upstream_ligands <- base::union(top_ligands_focused_set, top_ligands_agnostic_set)
    shared_ligands         <- base::intersect(top_ligands_focused_set, top_ligands_agnostic_set)
    
    # --- Plot 1: actividad de ligandos por sender ---
    top_ligands_plot <- ligand_activities_by_sender %>%
      dplyr::group_by(sender) %>%
      dplyr::slice_max(aupr_corrected, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(is_shared = test_ligand %in% shared_ligands)
    
    p_ligand_activity <- ggplot(top_ligands_plot,
                                aes(x = reorder(test_ligand, aupr_corrected), y = aupr_corrected,
                                    fill = sender, alpha = is_shared)) +
      geom_col() +
      coord_flip() +
      facet_wrap(~ sender, scales = "free_y") +
      scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1, `FALSE` = 0.55), guide = "none") +
      labs(
        x = "Ligand", y = "Predicted activity (corrected AUPR)",
        title = paste0("Candidate ligands by sender celltype -> hub genes of module ",
                       module_oi, " in ", receiver_oi),
        subtitle = "Target gene set = module hub genes (top kME); solid bars = also top-ranked sender-agnostic"
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
      theme(legend.position = "none")
    
    if (verbose) print(p_ligand_activity)
    ggsave(
      paste0("plot_ligand_activity_hubgenes_", module_oi, "_", receiver_oi, ".pdf"),
      p_ligand_activity, width = 10, height = 7
    )
    
    # --- Plot 2: heatmap ligando-target ---
    active_ligand_target_links_df <- best_upstream_ligands %>%
      lapply(get_weighted_ligand_target_links,
             geneset              = geneset_oi,
             ligand_target_matrix = ligand_target_matrix,
             n                    = 100) %>%
      bind_rows() %>%
      tidyr::drop_na()
    
    p_ligand_target_heatmap <- NULL
    if (nrow(active_ligand_target_links_df) > 0) {
      active_ligand_target_links <- prepare_ligand_target_visualization(
        ligand_target_df     = active_ligand_target_links_df,
        ligand_target_matrix = ligand_target_matrix,
        cutoff               = 1/3
      )
      
      order_ligands <- intersect(best_upstream_ligands, colnames(active_ligand_target_links)) %>% rev()
      order_targets <- active_ligand_target_links_df$target %>%
        unique() %>%
        intersect(rownames(active_ligand_target_links))
      
      vis_ligand_target <- active_ligand_target_links[order_targets, order_ligands, drop = FALSE]
      
      p_ligand_target_heatmap <- vis_ligand_target %>%
        make_heatmap_ggplot(
          y_name       = paste0("Hub genes of module ", module_oi, " (", receiver_oi, ")"),
          x_name       = "Prioritized ligands (sender-focused U sender-agnostic)",
          color        = "purple",
          legend_title = "Regulatory\npotential"
        ) +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(face = "italic", angle = 90, hjust = 1))
      
      if (verbose) print(p_ligand_target_heatmap)
      ggsave(
        paste0("plot_ligand_target_heatmap_", module_oi, "_", receiver_oi, ".pdf"),
        p_ligand_target_heatmap, width = 10, height = 8
      )
    } else {
      cat("  -> Ningún link ligando-target pasó el cutoff para", module_oi, "/", receiver_oi,
          "-- se salta el heatmap.\n")
    }
    
    # --- Ligando top único + tabla de sus genes target ---
    top_ligand <- dplyr::bind_rows(
      ligand_activities_by_sender %>% dplyr::select(test_ligand, aupr_corrected),
      if (!is.null(ligand_activities_agnostic)) {
        ligand_activities_agnostic %>% dplyr::select(test_ligand, aupr_corrected)
      } else NULL
    ) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(desc(aupr_corrected)) %>%
      dplyr::slice(1) %>%
      dplyr::pull(test_ligand)
    
    active_ligand_targets <- get_weighted_ligand_target_links(
      ligand               = top_ligand,
      geneset              = geneset_oi,
      ligand_target_matrix = ligand_target_matrix,
      n                    = 100
    )
    
    # --- Plot 3: heatmap ligando-receptor ---
    local_lr_network <- lr_network
    if (!"from" %in% colnames(local_lr_network) && "ligand" %in% colnames(local_lr_network)) {
      local_lr_network <- local_lr_network %>% dplyr::rename(from = ligand, to = receptor)
    }
    
    ligand_receptor_links_df <- get_weighted_ligand_receptor_links(
      best_upstream_ligands,
      expressed_receptors,
      local_lr_network,
      weighted_networks$lr_sig
    )
    
    p_ligand_receptor_heatmap <- NULL
    if (nrow(ligand_receptor_links_df) > 0) {
      vis_ligand_receptor_network <- prepare_ligand_receptor_visualization(
        ligand_receptor_links_df,
        best_upstream_ligands,
        order_hclust = "both"
      )
      
      p_ligand_receptor_heatmap <- t(vis_ligand_receptor_network) %>%
        make_heatmap_ggplot(
          y_name       = "Ligands",
          x_name       = paste0("Receptors expressed in receiver (", receiver_oi, ")"),
          color        = "mediumvioletred",
          legend_title = "Prior interaction\npotential"
        ) +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(face = "italic", angle = 90, hjust = 1))
      
      if (verbose) print(p_ligand_receptor_heatmap)
      ggsave(
        paste0("plot_ligand_receptor_heatmap_", module_oi, "_", receiver_oi, ".pdf"),
        p_ligand_receptor_heatmap, width = 9, height = 7
      )
      
      write.csv(
        ligand_receptor_links_df,
        paste0("ligand_receptor_links_", module_oi, "_", receiver_oi, ".csv"),
        row.names = FALSE
      )
    } else {
      cat("  -> No se encontraron links ligando-receptor para", module_oi, "/", receiver_oi, ".\n")
    }
    
    # --- Plot 4: signaling path (ligando -> receptor -> TF -> target hub gene) ---
    p_signaling_path  <- NULL
    sig_path_combined <- NULL
    if (nrow(active_ligand_targets) > 0) {
      top_target_for_path <- active_ligand_targets %>%
        dplyr::arrange(desc(weight)) %>%
        dplyr::slice(1) %>%
        dplyr::pull(target)
      
      sig_path <- tryCatch(
        get_ligand_signaling_path(
          ligand_tf_matrix  = ligand_tf_matrix,
          ligands_all       = top_ligand,
          targets_all       = top_target_for_path,
          top_n_regulators  = 4,
          weighted_networks = weighted_networks,
          minmax_scaling    = TRUE
        ),
        error = function(e) {
          message("  [", module_oi, "/", receiver_oi, "] Signaling path inference falló (",
                  conditionMessage(e), ")")
          NULL
        }
      )
      
      if (!is.null(sig_path) && nrow(sig_path$sig) + nrow(sig_path$gr) > 0) {
        sig_path_combined <- dplyr::bind_rows(sig_path$sig, sig_path$gr)
        sig_graph <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(sig_path_combined, directed = TRUE)
        
        p_signaling_path <- ggraph::ggraph(sig_graph, layout = "kk") +
          ggraph::geom_edge_link(
            aes(edge_width = weight, edge_alpha = weight),
            arrow   = grid::arrow(length = unit(3, "mm"), type = "closed"),
            end_cap = ggraph::circle(3, "mm"),
            color   = "grey50"
          ) +
          ggraph::geom_node_point(size = 5, color = "steelblue") +
          ggraph::geom_node_text(aes(label = name), repel = TRUE, size = 3) +
          ggraph::scale_edge_width(range = c(0.5, 2)) +
          theme_void() +
          labs(title = paste("Signaling path:", top_ligand, "->", top_target_for_path),
               subtitle = paste0("Module ", module_oi, " hub gene, receiver = ", receiver_oi))
        
        if (verbose) print(p_signaling_path)
        ggsave(
          paste0("plot_signaling_path_", module_oi, "_", receiver_oi, "_",
                 top_ligand, "_", top_target_for_path, ".pdf"),
          p_signaling_path, width = 8, height = 6
        )
      } else {
        cat("  -> No se pudo inferir signaling path para", module_oi, "/", receiver_oi,
            "(", top_ligand, "->", top_target_for_path, ").\n")
      }
    } else {
      cat("  -> active_ligand_targets vacío para", module_oi, "/", receiver_oi,
          "-- no hay target para trazar signaling path.\n")
    }
    
    list(
      module_oi                   = module_oi,
      receiver_oi                 = receiver_oi,
      geneset_oi                  = geneset_oi,
      background_expressed_genes  = background_expressed_genes,
      ligand_activities_by_sender = ligand_activities_by_sender,
      ligand_activities_agnostic  = ligand_activities_agnostic,
      best_upstream_ligands       = best_upstream_ligands,
      shared_ligands              = shared_ligands,
      top_ligand                  = top_ligand,
      active_ligand_targets       = active_ligand_targets,
      sig_path_combined           = sig_path_combined,
      p_ligand_activity           = p_ligand_activity,
      p_ligand_target_heatmap     = p_ligand_target_heatmap,
      p_ligand_receptor_heatmap   = p_ligand_receptor_heatmap,
      p_signaling_path            = p_signaling_path
    )
    
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("  [", module_oi, "/", receiver_oi,
            "] run_candidate_plots fallo con un error no controlado: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  })
  
  return(result)
}
```

### Candidato principal (`top_hit`)

Se corre primero para el candidato principal seleccionado por `SELECTION_METRIC`; sus resultados se asignan a las variables globales `ligand_activities_by_sender` / `ligand_activities_agnostic` que usan las secciones de más abajo (golden table, heatmap general, export multi-hoja), igual que en la versión anterior.

```{r hub-genes-top-hit-run, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
TOP_N_LIGANDS<-10
top_hit_result <- run_candidate_plots(module_oi, receiver_oi)

if (is.null(top_hit_result)) {
  stop("El candidato top_hit (", module_oi, "/", receiver_oi,
       ") no produjo resultados válidos -- revisa geneset_oi/background.")
}

geneset_oi                  <- top_hit_result$geneset_oi
background_expressed_genes  <- top_hit_result$background_expressed_genes
ligand_activities_by_sender <- top_hit_result$ligand_activities_by_sender
ligand_activities_agnostic  <- top_hit_result$ligand_activities_agnostic
best_upstream_ligands       <- top_hit_result$best_upstream_ligands
shared_ligands               <- top_hit_result$shared_ligands
top_ligand                  <- top_hit_result$top_ligand
active_ligand_targets       <- top_hit_result$active_ligand_targets

cat("\nCandidatos ligandos top (sender-focused, cualquier sender celltype) para el programa hub del módulo",
    module_oi, "en", receiver_oi, ":\n")
print(head(ligand_activities_by_sender, 15))

if (!is.null(ligand_activities_agnostic)) {
  cat("\nCandidatos ligandos top (sender-agnostic) para el mismo programa hub:\n")
  print(head(ligand_activities_agnostic, 15))
}

cat("\nLigandos compartidos por AMBOS enfoques (candidatos más fuertes):\n")
print(shared_ligands)
```

### Todos los candidatos: mismos gráficos, en loop

Se repite exactamente el mismo bloque de análisis y gráficos de arriba (actividad de ligandos por sender, heatmap ligando-target, heatmap ligando-receptor, signaling path) para **cada fila** de `module_celltype_candidates` -- no solo para `top_hit`. Cada candidato genera su propio set de PDFs/CSVs (ya nombrados por `module_oi`/`receiver_oi`, así que no se pisan entre sí). Los resultados de todos los candidatos quedan además en `all_candidates_results` (lista con un elemento por module x celltype) para inspección posterior en R sin tener que releer los CSVs.

```{r hub-genes-all-candidates-loop, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
cat("Candidatos a procesar en el loop:", nrow(module_celltype_candidates), "\n")

all_candidates_results <- purrr::map2(
  module_celltype_candidates$module,
  module_celltype_candidates$celltype,
  run_candidate_plots
)
names(all_candidates_results) <- paste(
  module_celltype_candidates$module, module_celltype_candidates$celltype, sep = "_"
)

# Candidatos que se saltaron (geneset_oi < 5 genes o ligand activity fallida en todos los senders)
skipped_candidates <- names(all_candidates_results)[vapply(all_candidates_results, is.null, logical(1))]
if (length(skipped_candidates) > 0) {
  cat("\nCandidatos sin resultados (geneset_oi < 5 genes o sin ligand activities válidas):\n")
  print(skipped_candidates)
}

# Tabla resumen: mejor ligando y su AUPR corregido por cada candidato procesado
all_candidates_results_ok <- Filter(Negate(is.null), all_candidates_results)

candidates_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(all_candidates_results_ok, function(res) {
  tibble::tibble(
    module            = res$module_oi,
    celltype          = res$receiver_oi,
    n_hub_genes       = length(res$geneset_oi),
    n_best_upstream   = length(res$best_upstream_ligands),
    n_shared_ligands  = length(res$shared_ligands),
    top_ligand        = res$top_ligand,
    top_ligand_aupr   = max(
      dplyr::bind_rows(
        res$ligand_activities_by_sender %>% dplyr::select(test_ligand, aupr_corrected),
        if (!is.null(res$ligand_activities_agnostic)) {
          res$ligand_activities_agnostic %>% dplyr::select(test_ligand, aupr_corrected)
        } else NULL
      )$aupr_corrected,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )
})

write.csv(candidates_summary, "all_candidates_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nResumen de todos los candidatos procesados (guardado en all_candidates_summary.csv):\n")
print(candidates_summary)
```

## Summary & Integration: Golden Table, Heatmaps, and Multi-sheet Export

### 1. Build the consolidated "golden table"

The golden table is a single denormalized data frame where every row is a unique ligand-receptor pair, enriched with: the contrasts where it was prioritized, module membership, SASP annotation, and top predicted ligand activity across all sender-celltype combinations. This is the table to use for filtering, sorting, and publication-quality figures.

```{r golden-table-build}
# Start with all prioritized LR pairs
golden_table <- multinichenet_output$prioritization_tables$group_prioritization_tbl %>%
  distinct(sender, receiver, ligand, receptor)

# Which contrasts contain each LR pair (pivot to comma-separated string)
lr_per_contrast <- multinichenet_output$prioritization_tables$group_prioritization_tbl %>%
  distinct(contrast, sender, receiver, ligand, receptor) %>%
  group_by(sender, receiver, ligand, receptor) %>%
  summarise(contrasts_active = paste(sort(unique(contrast)), collapse = "; "),
            n_contrasts = n_distinct(contrast), .groups = "drop")

golden_table <- golden_table %>%
  left_join(lr_per_contrast, by = c("sender", "receiver", "ligand", "receptor"))

# WGCNA module membership: ligand in sender cell type?
# ============================================================
# {r golden-table-build}  -- ligand_modules / receptor_modules
# ============================================================
ligand_modules <- gene_celltype_module %>%
  filter(module %in% age_associated_modules) %>%   # antes: significant_modules
  group_by(gene, celltype) %>%
  summarise(module = paste(sort(unique(module)), collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename(ligand = gene, sender = celltype, ligand_modules = module)

receptor_modules <- gene_celltype_module %>%
  filter(module %in% age_associated_modules) %>%   # antes: significant_modules
  group_by(gene, celltype) %>%
  summarise(module = paste(sort(unique(module)), collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename(receptor = gene, receiver = celltype, receptor_modules = module)



# Top ligand activity for this LR pair (across all senders/receivers)
if (nrow(ligand_activities_by_sender) > 0) {
  top_ligand_activity <- ligand_activities_by_sender %>%
    group_by(test_ligand) %>%
    slice_max(aupr_corrected, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    rename(ligand = test_ligand, max_aupr_corrected = aupr_corrected, aupr_sender_ct = sender) %>%
    dplyr::select(ligand, max_aupr_corrected, aupr_sender_ct)

  golden_table <- golden_table %>%
    left_join(top_ligand_activity, by = c("ligand"))
}

# Sort by activity (if available) or by n_contrasts
golden_table <- golden_table %>%
  arrange(desc(max_aupr_corrected %||% 0), desc(n_contrasts))

cat("Golden table built:", nrow(golden_table), "unique LR pairs\n")
print(head(golden_table, 10))

write.csv(golden_table, "golden_table_LR_pairs.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

### 2. Ligand activity heatmap (all ligands × sender cell types)

A heatmap showing which ligands are active (high aupr_corrected) in which sender cell types. Restricted to top 30 ligands for readability.

```{r ligand-activity-heatmap, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
heatmap_data <- ligand_activities_by_sender %>%
  dplyr::select(test_ligand, sender, aupr_corrected) %>%
  group_by(test_ligand, sender) %>%
  slice_max(aupr_corrected, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(aupr_corrected)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 30)

p_ligand_heatmap <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = sender, y = reorder(test_ligand, aupr_corrected),
                                              fill = aupr_corrected)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#fee5d9", high = "#a50f15") +
  labs(
    x = "Sender cell type",
    y = "Ligand",
    fill = "AUPR (corrected)",
    title = "Ligand Activity Heatmap",
    subtitle = "Top 30 ligands by max activity; color = predicted activity for receptor target genes"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

print(p_ligand_heatmap)
ggsave("plot_ligand_activity_heatmap_top30.pdf", p_ligand_heatmap, width = 12, height = 8)
```

### 3. Network plot of cell-cell communication (interactive visNetwork)

An interactive network where nodes are cell types and edges represent LR pairs. Edge width = number of distinct ligand-receptor pairs; edge color reflects the proportion of pairs overlapping age-associated WGCNA modules.

```{r network-visualization, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
library(tidyverse)
library(visNetwork)

network_summary <- golden_table %>%
  group_by(sender, receiver) %>%
  summarise(
    n_pairs       = n(),
    n_wgcna       = sum(!is.na(ligand_modules) | !is.na(receptor_modules)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Evitamos división por cero o NaNs asegurando que n_pairs > 0
    pct_wgcna = if_else(n_pairs > 0, 100 * n_wgcna / n_pairs, 0),
    # Reemplazamos cualquier NA residual por 0
    pct_wgcna = replace_na(pct_wgcna, 0)
  )

network_nodes <- unique(c(network_summary$sender, network_summary$receiver))

nodes_df <- data.frame(
  id    = network_nodes,
  label = network_nodes,
  title = network_nodes,
  color = "#2c7fb8",
  size  = 30
)

# Creamos el gradiente de forma segura controlando el rango de colores
edge_colors <- colorRamp(c("lightgrey", "#2ca25f"))(pmin(pmax(network_summary$pct_wgcna / 100, 0), 1))

# Manejo seguro por si quedara algún elemento nulo (asegurando dimensiones de matriz)
if (is.matrix(edge_colors)) {
  edge_colors[is.na(edge_colors)] <- 200 
  edge_colors_hex <- apply(edge_colors, 1, function(x) rgb(x[1], x[2], x[3], maxColorValue = 255))
} else {
  edge_colors_hex <- rep("#d3d3d3", nrow(network_summary))
}

# Construcción de los bordes (edges_df) requeridos por visNetwork a partir del resumen
edges_df <- data.frame(
  from  = network_summary$sender,
  to    = network_summary$receiver,
  value = network_summary$n_pairs,
  color = edge_colors_hex,
  title = paste0("Pairs: ", network_summary$n_pairs, "<br>WGCNA %: ", round(network_summary$pct_wgcna, 1), "%")
)

p_network <- visNetwork(nodes_df, edges_df, directed = TRUE, physics = TRUE) %>%
  visLayout(randomSeed = 42) %>%
  visOptions(highlightNearest = TRUE, nodesIdSelection = TRUE) %>%
  visPhysics(enabled = TRUE, stabilization = list(iterations = 200))

visSave(p_network, "network_LR_celltype_interactive.html")
cat("Interactive network saved to: network_LR_celltype_interactive.html\n")
```

### 5. Export all key tables to multi-sheet Excel workbook

```{r excel-export}
# Clean up list columns for Excel compatibility
golden_table_export <- golden_table %>% 
  mutate(across(where(is.list), ~ as.character(.)))

# Build workbook with multiple sheets
wb <- createWorkbook()

sheet_data <- list(
  "Golden_Table"              = golden_table_export,
  "LR_WGCNA_Overlap"          = lr_prioritized_annotated, 
  "GO_Overlap_Terms"          = go_overlap_combined %>%
    dplyr::select(any_of(c("Description", "module", "p.adjust", "n_overlap_genes", "go_source"))),
  "Ligand_Activity"           = ligand_activities_by_sender %>%
    dplyr::select(any_of(c("test_ligand", "sender", "aupr", "aupr_corrected", "p_value", "p.value"))),
  "Ligand_Activity_Agnostic"  = if (!is.null(ligand_activities_agnostic)) {
    ligand_activities_agnostic %>% dplyr::select(any_of(c("test_ligand", "aupr", "aupr_corrected", "p_value", "p.value")))
  } else data.frame(),
  "Ligand_Receptor_Links"     = ligand_receptor_links_df,
  "Ligand_Activity_Robustness" = robustness_results %>%
    dplyr::select(any_of(c("test_ligand", "sender", "receiver", "module", "aupr_corrected")))
)

# Add sheets with formatting
for (sheet_name in names(sheet_data)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)

  if (is.null(sheet_data[[sheet_name]]) || ncol(sheet_data[[sheet_name]]) == 0) {
    writeData(wb, sheet = sheet_name, x = "No data available for this section")
    next
  }

  writeData(wb, sheet = sheet_name, x = sheet_data[[sheet_name]])

  # Style headers
  headerStyle <- createStyle(
    fgFill = "#2c7fb8", fontColour = "white", textDecoration = "bold", halign = "center"
  )
  addStyle(wb, sheet = sheet_name, style = headerStyle, rows = 1,
           cols = 1:ncol(sheet_data[[sheet_name]]))
  setColWidths(wb, sheet = sheet_name, cols = 1:ncol(sheet_data[[sheet_name]]), widths = "auto")
  freezePane(wb, sheet = sheet_name, firstRow = TRUE)
}

saveWorkbook(wb, "multinichenet_wgcna_integration_tables.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
cat("Multi-sheet Excel export saved to: multinichenet_wgcna_integration_tables.xlsx\n")
```
